reason: The one-entry helper proposals are the same experiment: the supplied feasibility review gives a concrete path to reuse its 64 KiB scratch while avoiding repeated helper calls and SME transitions. The 16-call wrapper did not show a repeatable gain, so that history does not establish whether the one-entry change helps. The 64 KiB full512 lifetime proposal directly targets allocation size but needs a risky packing and compute reorder; it reduces peak scratch, not total packed data. The three two-K loop proposals describe the same control simplification, so they should not be treated as distinct experiments. Panel packing adds allocation and copy work, while transpose fusion has high assembly risk without reducing total A packing work. The transpose-descriptor proposal also needs a generated primitive that is unavailable. No supplied measurement demonstrates a gain for any proposal or establishes causality from noisy scores.
